message.content:
Here are some of the most popular and highly regarded sushi restaurants in Tokyo:

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights |
|------------|----------|------------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Ginza (Tokyo) | Legendary chef Jiro Ono; Michelin‑starred; famed for precision and quality. |
| **Sushi Saito** | Minato | Intimate setting, 3 Michelin stars; known for meticulous preparation and seasonal ingredients. |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Ginza | 3 Michelin stars; offers a refined omakase experience with a focus on subtle flavors. |
| **Sushi Mizutani** | Ginza | 2 Michelin stars; celebrated for its fresh fish and elegant presentation. |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Popular spot for fresh tuna and other sashimi; long lines but worth the wait. |
| **Sushi Zanmai** | Multiple locations | Casual chain with a wide selection; great for a quick, high‑quality bite. |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | Known for its traditional approach and excellent customer service. |
| **Sushi Sawada** | Ginza | 2 Michelin stars; focuses on seasonal ingredients and a minimalist menu. |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Ginza | 1 Michelin star; offers a more affordable yet still exceptional omakase. |
| **Sushi Tsubaki** | Shinjuku | 2 Michelin stars; renowned for its creative takes on classic nigiri. |

These restaurants range from high‑end, Michelin‑starred establishments to more casual, yet still top‑quality spots. If you’re planning a visit, it’s wise to make reservations well in advance—especially for the Michelin‑starred venues. Enjoy your sushi adventure!
